topic: Holomorphic Dynamics: The Art of Iterated Chaos
target_audience: Undergraduate students in STEM or advanced high school students with a background in complex numbers

sections.title: The Canvas: The Complex Plane and the Feedback Loop
lecture_lines: Complex numbers represent points on a 2D plane.
Iteration creates a mathematical feedback loop.
The output of one step becomes the next input.
Points jump across the plane following this rule.
Holomorphic Dynamics studies these paths over time.
animations: Create a coordinate plane. Place a point at (1, 0.5) labeled 'z = a + bi' in #FFFFFF.
Draw a curved arrow from the point back to itself through a box labeled 'f(z)' to show feedback.
Show a sequence of points z0, z1, z2, z3 appearing as the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pixel.svg] jumps on the plane.
Highlight the path (orbit) connecting these points with a #FFFF00 line.
Fade out the plane and keep only the orbit, emphasizing the study of 'Holomorphic Dynamics'.

sections.title: The Iteration Machine: z² + c
lecture_lines: We focus on the simple rule: z squared plus c.
Squaring magnitude stretches or shrinks the point.
Adding c shifts the point in a specific direction.
animations: Display the formula 'f(z) = z² + c' in #00FFFF at the top center.
Animate a point z squaring (scaling and rotating) through a machine [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/machine.svg] followed by a vector translation by 'c'.
Show two distinct paths: a stable spiral inward (#00FF00) and an unstable path outward (#FF0000).

sections.title: Stability vs. Chaos: Fatou and Julia Sets
lecture_lines: Fatou sets contain points with stable, predictable paths.
Nearby points in these regions stay together.
Julia sets form the chaotic boundaries between them.
On the boundary, tiny changes lead to chaos.
This edge of chaos creates intricate beauty.
animations: Fill the background with a fractal-like boundary in #FFD700 to represent a Julia set.
Place two #FFFFFF dots extremely close to each other on the boundary.
Animate their paths: one stays in a smooth region, the other diverges wildly.
Label the smooth, predictable regions 'Fatou Set' in #ADD8E6.
Label the intricate boundary 'Julia Set' in #FFD700.

sections.title: The Master Map: The Mandelbrot Set
lecture_lines: The Mandelbrot set maps all possible c values.
Black regions represent c values with connected Julia sets.
It serves as a dictionary for all complex behaviors.
animations: Draw the Mandelbrot set shape in #222222 with a #FFFFFF outline on the complex 'c-plane' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/map.svg].
Contrast a point 'c' inside (pulsing #00FF00) with a point 'c' outside (pulsing #FF0000).
Show the transition between a connected Julia set and a disconnected 'dust' Julia set for these points [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/dictionary.svg].

sections.title: Self-Similarity and the Infinite Zoom
lecture_lines: These boundaries reveal intricate, repeating fractal structures.
Zooming in reveals tiny, perfect copies of the whole.
Local shapes are preserved while global views are distorted.
This infinite self-similarity defines the beauty of holomorphic dynamics.
Simple rules generate infinite, self-repeating complexity.
animations: Focus on a specific 'bulb' on the edge of the Mandelbrot set boundary.
Perform a smooth, continuous zoom into the boundary's intricate details.
Reveal a 'Mini-Mandelbrot' (#00FF00) that is identical to the original set.
Highlight repeating spiral structures in #FF00FF as the zoom progresses.
Display the text 'Infinite Complexity' in #FFFFFF as the final zoom level is reached.
